title: User JWT Auth Governance Large-Diff Reliability

phases.objective: Run the centralized fail-closed User JWT governance scan across a large baseline-to-head diff without child-process buffer exhaustion while preserving every existing auth rule and fail-closed decision.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The official user-jwt-auth-governance.mjs command on the exact pull-request head with origin/main as its explicit baseline
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The full large repository diff is scanned through the bounded Git subprocess, the guard reports zero violations for the candidate, and no ENOBUFS or rule bypass occurs.
steps: Validate that the Git subprocess buffer is bounded at 64 MiB and is wired into the same helper used by baseline-to-head scanning.
Execute the official User JWT auth governance command against origin/main on the exact candidate head.
Retain all hardened-file, secret-fallback, route-local-guard, and route-local-jsonwebtoken-import checks unchanged.
Return the normal fail-closed result without reading GitHub Job logs or exposing source evidence beyond the existing annotations.
assertions: The governed Git helper uses GIT_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES equal to 64 MiB.
The baseline-to-head diff continues through the same governed Git helper.
The official scan completes without ENOBUFS on the current large Rollup diff.
The official scan reports zero User JWT auth violations on the candidate head.
No JWT governance rule, protected file list, runtime authorization behavior, secret boundary, provider dispatch, migration, deployment, or Production authority changes.

phases.objective: Retain exact-head structured CI evidence that the official guard completes on future large Rollup diffs without buffer exhaustion.
Exercise bounded failure behavior for malformed Git refs, unavailable baselines, and diffs larger than the configured safety ceiling.
This is a repository CI governance reliability change and performs no live canary.
This change grants no deployment, provider, migration, or Production authority.
